purpose: WELL-134 bounded FP-001 EN/AF development sign-in and current-session protected access. This source map grants no release or review approval. WELL-163 adds a current-use Session inventory and revocation of one other Session on the same Account. WELL-170 adds development-only global sign-out with fresh purpose-bound password and applicable TOTP proof. WELL-177 adds a bounded self-display of the presenting Session holder's current Platform Member Reference in English and Afrikaans.

implementation_revision.semantics: Snapshot of the committed WELL-134 application and proof source. This map is descriptive; inspect current source, routed authority and live Plane before reuse. WELL-134 author review strengthens the shared browser boundary: all endpoint events are redacted, legal routes avoid router telemetry, unknown routes fail closed, and parsing/method handling runs inside bounded class-only failure handling. Master Gate AC-12 correction verifies the same artifact bytes before embedding and both pinned sources at compile time, retaining runtime fail-closed eligibility. Ordinary browser proof now doubles computed text sizes at each of five widths and restores inline styles. WELL-112 preserves both session CSP directives, the owning sign-in interfaces and the encrypted Identity cookie transport. The shared endpoint/boundary isolates the DEV-only guide with a fresh rendering connection and a cookie-free, origin-checked LiveView transport. The normal /live socket and sign-in controller dispatch remain unchanged. WELL-114 changes test observations only: fixture queries filter before hydration, registration inputs are unique, and global Session/token maintenance proofs use rollback to preserve retained data. Business ownership and lifecycle are unchanged. Source-linked proof and refreshed hashes do not certify runtime completion, merge or resulting main. WELL-136 refreshes shared source references after independent semantic review; this mapped capability remains unchanged. WELL-156 refreshes locators in shared source files. The new ordinary primary-email-change routes and context do not change this capability contract. The WELL-156 correction refreshes its shared source locators. WELL-143 extends shared TEST creation ownership to MessageIntent and Session identifiers. Magic request observations and full-row Token/Session fingerprints exclude independent fixtures while retaining unexpected owned consequences. Maintenance proof separately checks foreign expired rows are restored after actual global maintenance rollback. P815 retains reset operation and account identifiers before JTI-based delivery. Production lifecycle and fixed proof inventory are unchanged; this evidence does not clear the unresolved P809 canonical failure. WELL-86 scopes interrupted Session issuance rollback to creation-owned full-row Token/Session fingerprints and retains failed assertion labels with boolean matches before raising. Permanent independent-owner and unexpected-owned-consequence tests preserve all existing guards and foreign rows. Backend absence is observed separately; no wait or retry is added. This repairs a demonstrated false-inclusion mechanism, without claiming attribution of historical intermittent failures or canonical success. WELL-163 adds a bounded EN/AF participant Session inventory and individual remote revocation with material Audit E2. WELL-170 serializes global termination with issuance under the Account lock, reuses reset's linked-token and device invalidation actions, and establishes Audit E2 within the same transaction. The PR #292 review follow-up extends the proof without changing the application transaction or policy. WELL-177 adds a current self-only PMR projection inside the existing Account, Token and Session lock boundary. The protected browser response displays the projection in the selected locale with a local clipboard control. The protected controller removes the PMR assign after Phoenix renders and before sending so Bandit request telemetry cannot retain the reference. WELL-187 adds locale-exact ordinary Recovery discovery to sign-in, gated by the existing Recovery entry and approved Content reader. WELL-189 refreshes shared source references. The mapped behavior is unchanged. WELL-210 refreshes the shared browser proof source references after the Recovery packet path moved to v0.3.0. The mapped behavior is unchanged.

request_flow.summary: Cold start: inspect the entry and Content gates, then password/magic controllers, then Identity interfaces and their owner transactions. Shell components render no Account, PMR or bearer context.

Normal authorized development navigation starts at registration entry and exposes locale-specific /login. The normal entry flag suffices with legacy browser-proof flags disabled. Verification still creates no Session and only offers sign-in.

Signed-out EN/AF sign-in offers a separate ordinary Recovery link when the existing bounded route and exact Content are eligible. The link carries the selected locale and opens the read-only Recovery request form.

Password POST delegates to Identity.authenticate_password/2. Success renews and clears the encrypted browser session, then stores transport credentials and locale and redirects to /session/protected. Failure renders one approved generic response with empty password.

Magic request delegates to Identity/Communications; neutral pending UI offers retry. Passive confirmation renders an explicit POST form. Successful consumption uses the same Session issuance and protected destination with magic provenance.
Protected GET always calls authorize_session. Denial clears transport state and renders usable reauthentication. No unfinished product destination or administrative capability is added.
Logout commits the current owner transition before transport drop and confirmed text. Error returns 503 with retry and sign-in links, without claiming durable logout.

WELL-163 cold start: follow the protected page link through RegistrationBoundary GET /session/manage or POST /session/manage/revoke, then SessionManagementController, Content load and Identity. List is an Account-scoped active keyset page of at most 20 rows with a linked unexpired user Token and both Session deadlines. Render only the opaque control identifier, current marker and timestamps. Cancel refreshes via GET. POST revalidates and awaits the durable result before displaying success.

WELL-170 cold start: from /session/manage follow /session/manage/all. RegistrationBoundary dispatches passive GET/HEAD and CSRF-protected POST to SessionManagementController. The form binds to the presenting Session and projects the factor requirement. Identity proves the current password and active-factor TOTP when applicable, saves and consumes purpose-bound assurance in a single transaction, then reports confirmed success, confirmed failure or uncertainty. Success drops the browser session and renders exact localized copy with reauthentication.

The protected GET derives credentials from the cookie and calls Identity. After current Account, Token and Session authority checks, Identity projects just the valid active PMR of the canonical Account. The no-store page renders a selectable value and localized native copy button. A same-origin script copies the value locally, announces the result and clears the value on page hide before a back-forward cache restore rechecks authority.

side_effects: Set ended_at, clear step-up assurance and establish one material Audit E2 in the same transaction. Existing Token may still verify cryptographically while the Session authorizer denies it.

guards: Current eligible ordinary Account and matching active Token/Session with both deadlines. Fresh password and current TOTP for active MFA, then unexpired Session assurance bound to the global purpose and Account security/MFA versions. Pending MFA or active Support grant blocks the participant path.
side_effects: Terminate all own pre-boundary active Sessions, clear assurance, revoke only linked user tokens and terminate own trusted DeviceAssurance. Commit one E2 obligation in the source transaction.

security_invariants.summary: Only Identity owns authentication authority. Cookie/account_id/PMR/query intent cannot select another Account or grant unfinished capabilities. Current scoped privileged and Privacy purpose checks remain separate owner boundaries.

Exact C-01 v0.1 is development-only. Both pinned artifact and approval hashes are checked before embedding; decoding uses the exact bytes that passed verification. Runtime consumption rechecks both current source hashes. Compile-time tampering followed by restoration cannot admit unapproved embedded text. Original canonical digest 43ee2ad61accfed40aceaa8fcb035c01282210a3ac69f5949df6c913419ccc5b is preserved as source identity, not claimed as the derived serialization hash. Missing/changed/withdrawn artifact fails closed with no fallback.
Compile-time production exclusion defeats all runtime development flags. The existing normal entry legal/content gate is retained; Content.EntryCopy is not expanded to the candidate registry.

Existing encrypted Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite cookie, renewal, CSRF, no-store/no-referrer and strict proof CSP remain. Password/protected pages permit same-origin connections for existing reload proof, with default-src none and no external connections.

No bearer/password enters ordinary rows, jobs, telemetry, referrers, assets or third-party requests. TEST email delivery reads only the real provider's transient payload and returns fixed boolean proof facts.

Endpoint start/stop always use the existing redacted connection projection because cookies accompany ordinary URLs. Legal GET/HEAD dispatch through the existing browser boundary. Unknown paths return 404; malformed JSON/query input returns its safe parser status with class-only logging, avoiding full-connection router/error telemetry. Parser, method override and HEAD order is retained inside the existing boundary; Session transport remains in Endpoint.

The DEV/test design guide renders on a fresh request projection with no Identity session, headers, cookies or endpoint secret. Its separate LiveView transport reads no session and enforces connection-origin checks. It grants no sign-in or protected-access capability. Reassess transport isolation before routing another LiveView.

The route requires bounded development, exact copy and the owning Identity interface. Foreign, unknown and self targets share an unavailable outcome. No raw credentials, JTI, device fingerprint or IP are projected; existing encryption and request telemetry exclusions still apply.
The global purpose cannot admit a privileged grant and trusted-device state cannot satisfy step-up. No password, OTP, bearer or device fingerprint enters Audit or a result body.

Self-display denies inactive or held Accounts, unverified email, invalid PMRs, stale or expired Session or Token authority, noncanonical or retired Accounts and mismatched credentials. It never resolves the survivor from a retired Account. The page excludes the reference from URLs and redacted endpoint telemetry.

concurrency.summary: Existing Account lock arbitrates password issuance against hold/credential change. Protected authorization locks Account, Token, Session in existing order and rechecks. Logout retains existing terminal Session serialization.

Magic issue/supersession/consume serialize on Account then current proof. Consumption and Session issuance share one transaction with unique provenance, so two consumers cannot commit two Sessions. No new process-local authority, scheduler or event model.

The Account lock orders remote revocation against issuance, password reset and hold. The initiating and target rows are rechecked under lock. Terminal state and the existing unique Audit source operation/type identity prevent duplicate effects; direct current logout still terminalizes under its own existing Session lock.

Global revocation locks the Account, then linked user Tokens in JTI order before locking the presenting Session. It revokes current Sessions and trusted devices inside the same transaction. Issuance committed ahead of the Account lock is revoked, and issuance behind the boundary rechecks eligibility and survives.

Self-display uses the same Account, presenting Token and Session locks as protected Session authorization. Concurrent requests can refresh ordinary Session activity and return the same reference when eligible. They do not allocate or update Account PMRs.

idempotency_retry.summary: Same magic operation retry reuses its proof identity and expiry; new operation supersedes current proof. Explicit consumption is single use. Separate valid password submissions remain separate authentications.

Repeated logout of logged_out is owner-idempotent and preserves ended_at; revoked/expired authority cannot be restored. Lost logout response may safely retry with the previous cookie; a denied browser converges through protected reauthentication.

A retry with a current initiating Session can observe an already-ended same-Account target. Unusable but still active targets return stale without changing state. Existing terminal time is immutable. No duplicate Audit obligation or materialized record.

A revoked presenting Session cannot produce another result or revoke fresh Sessions. The browser rejects a stale confirmation bound to another Session even with fresh browser CSRF. The single Audit operation is keyed by the consumed presenting Session.

failure_recovery.summary: Issuance or proof-consumption failure rolls back Token/Session/proof effects. A response lost after committed magic consumption cannot replay the proof; request a new link or sign in with the password. A lost password result requires fresh authentication, not inferred success.
Committed valid authority reconstructs on a fresh connection and BEAM instance. Revoked Token/Session, hold, expiry and logged_out remain denied after restart; cleanup retains Session history.

Owner unavailability renders neutral login/unavailable magic or explicit unconfirmed logout. No partial protected effect or claimed delivery success follows provider ambiguity. Existing reset/hold/recovery invalidators remain authoritative.

An Audit rejection rolls back the source and returns failure. With no confirmed transaction outcome, the browser presents uncertain copy and refreshes the current Identity read. Both source revocation and pending Audit work reconstruct from PostgreSQL.

A conflicting Audit obligation returns confirmed rollback. A database exception can report uncertainty even when durable reads establish rollback. The injected Audit insert fault preserves the prior MFA period and assurance, and the same current code succeeds after fault removal. Lost acknowledgement after commit yields the EN/AF uncertain response and durable revoked authority. A browser-level cut yields no completion claim. Fresh authentication and inventory reconcile the result.

safe_extensions.summary: Maintain this map when changing the capability. Extend only through current Domain interfaces, approved semantic copy identity and observed owner/browser regressions.

reuse.summary: USE existing Ash Resources/actions, AshAuthentication JWT/password verification, AshPostgres transactions/constraints and Phoenix forms. Signals and Temporal Resources are not applicable: this web slice adds no cross-Domain reaction or as-of/effective-period requirement. No dependency installation.

EXTEND existing Ash and AshAuthentication Session authority, reuse the terminal Ash update, compose Audit E2 with the current transaction, and reuse existing Phoenix forms and shell. No new storage authority or dependency. Signals and Temporal Resources do not fit the atomic obligation and current-state read.

prohibited_shortcuts.summary: No parallel authentication authority, custom Repo business writes, public bearer API, localStorage, admin bypass, new grant UI, scheduler, duration policy, production provider or unfinished participant function.

proof_limitations: WELL-132 exercises the real Identity enrollment and confirmation calls on either side of a controlled 30-second TOTP boundary. The test selects distinct adjacent codes, checks that stale rejection leaves the factor pending with no accepted period or confirmation obligation, then confirms with the current code. The Audit rollback test submits the same valid code at the same instant with and without the injected failure. The original failing runs did not capture the generation and validation instants.

The linked existing migrations establish Account foreign key, unique Session/Token and magic-provenance constraints. The retention migration removes the Token foreign key so cleanup preserves Session history. Existing rollback/reconciliation guards still apply.
Author proof and this map never substitute for exact-head independent Master Gate, hosted CI or resulting-main reconciliation. WELL-21 remains open.
